title.narrative: COVID-19: Active Response and Expenditure Support Program

description.narrative: The CARES Program aims to help the government in implementing its pandemic response plan the National Relief Program to respond to public health emergencies and to mitigate adverse economic and social impacts caused by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

Output: Economic support for affected sectors implemented Indicator: Concessional lending extended to at least 10,000 affected MSMEs, of which at least 30% are women-led MSMEs and at least 50% of women-led MSMEs are women from disadvantaged groups g Progress/Status: As reported by NRB the concessional loan extended to 129,680 MSMEs (53,785 for commercial agriculture and livestock businesses, 73,078 women entrepreneurs and remaining 1,817 borrowers in other sectors as of mid-October, 2021.
A total of NRs. 1.05 billion loan was approved under the business continuity loan scheme as of mid- October 2021. Data Source: Nepal Rastra Bank Banks and Financial Institution Statistics (monthly), banks' quarterly report to Nepal Rastra Bank Actual value:

Output: Health system response measures supported Indicator: Financial incentives provided to at least 70,000 health and frontline personnel responding to COVID-19, of whom at least 70% are women d Achievement: 14847 Progress/Status: 14,847 health and frontline personnel provided with financial incentives (8,999; 60.6% female) based on available data from 17 federal health institutions, 31 provincial and 114 Local Levels (LLs) as reported.
Report compilation from remaining federal and provincial institutions and local levels is in progress. Source: MOHP and MOFAGA Data Source: CARES Program semiannual progress report

Output: Social protection and relief programs delivered Indicator: Employment support provided through the Prime Minister's Employment Program to at least 500,000 unemployed people, comprising at least 50% women (including women returnee migrant workers) and 25% individuals from disadvantaged groups f Achievement: 277841 Progress/Status: Employment was provided for 104,050 persons (46,957 i.e. 45.13% female, and 62.4% disadvantaged group) on a wage basis in Fiscal Year 2019/20.
173,791 (47.7% female including women returnee migrant workers and 61.3% disadvantaged group) received employment from 16,660 projects, creating total employment of 13,203,358 days on a wage basis in the fiscal year 2020/2021 with an average 76 days per employee ((Source: PMEP/MOLESS, 17 November 2021). Data Source: CARES program semiannual progress report

Output: Social protection and relief programs delivered Indicator: Food assistance distributed to 1 million poor and vulnerable households.e Achievement: 1904365 Progress/Status: 1,904,365 households (5,511,814 people) have received food assistance5 so far (Source: CMIS-MOFAGA, 19 October 2021). Data Source: CARES program semiannual progress report

Output: Health system response measures supported Indicator: Quarantine space for at least 200,000 people with separate wards for women and men, set up in all 7 provinces c Achievement: 278143 Progress/Status: 6,304 quarantine centers with a bed capacity of 205,003 established as of the first week of July 2020.
278,143 people have returned home after using these quarantine facilities during the first and second surge of COVID-19. Among the users, 14.74% are female. (Crisis Management Information System (CMIS), MOFAGA, 19 October 2021)
‘Information received from 26 local levels (phone call survey at 11 local levels and field review at 15 local levels in March/April 2021) showed that separate wards for males and females were maintained in all the quarantine centers.' Data Source: CARES Program semiannual progress report
